title: How to get tretinoin through your AI, no subscription required
summary: Tretinoin online: compare Curology and Agency with a $40 FutureClinic visit, where a doctor reviews your case and can prescribe if it's right for you.
body_markdown:
Prescription tretinoin from Curology or Agency comes in a compounded bottle shipped every 60 days on a recurring subscription, and their clinicians focus on conditions on the company's menu.


On FutureClinic, no intake form gets approved in bulk. Instead, an individual physician reviews your entire history and photos and sends back a tailored treatment plan alongside a Human Signature, which is a brief voice or video message recorded live just for you.


Whenever you need a refill or a check-in months later, your messages go back to the same doctor in your ongoing thread, giving the two of you room to build trust, test different retinoid strengths, and see how your skin responds over time. Because FutureClinic sells no medicine and your physician earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, their only incentive is to help you. There is no subscription required, and if your doctor decides it's right for you, they can send whichever non-controlled generic or brand-name retinoid suits your skin best to the pharmacy you choose, whether that is a neighborhood drugstore or a mail-order service that ships to your home. That physician can also address other concerns within their specialty, and every FutureClinic physician you see works from your[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) so your history stays unified.


## How does FutureClinic compare with Curology and Agency for tretinoin?


The main difference is breadth. Curology treats[acne](https://futureclinic.com/blog/best-way-to-treat-acne-using-ai) , rosacea, skin aging, and certain hair loss, and states as of October 2026 that it does not treat eczema, vitiligo, or psoriasis, or prescribe isotretinoin. Agency treats skin aging and pigment. Both use physicians, physician assistants, or nurse practitioners. FutureClinic connects you with physicians only, meaning every clinician holds an MD, DO or MBBS degree rather than practicing as a nurse practitioner or a physician assistant. Our clinic has over 300 doctors. They span more than 60 specialties, generalists and specialists alike.


If you message a dermatologist for tretinoin and later develop eczema, psoriasis, or hair loss, that same doctor can help in the same chat; dermatologists who offer isotretinoin manage it by message, iPLEDGE included. Over months, the same doctor can guide you through an early 7-to-10-day acne flare, swap a gel for a cream in winter, or step from 0.025% to 0.05%. Should you later message a different FutureClinic physician in another field for an unrelated health issue, every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record.


Did you want a recurring compounded bottle plan and its rules, or your own dermatologist?


When do Curology, Agency, or Musely suit you better? If you want their compounded formulas priced into a 60-day schedule, they are strong options. Curology and Agency cover all 50 states and Washington, D.C.; as of October 2026, Curology offers a $5.45 trial and a $24.97 Walmart kit with no subscription, and Musely offers its compounded Acne Cream ($20 visit plus $30 a month or $86 once as of October 2026). For one-to-one physician care and standard pharmacy prescriptions, FutureClinic is the stronger fit.

## What does tretinoin cost over a year without a subscription?


A low monthly price for a custom bottle assumes you stay subscribed to keep getting refills. At $59.90 every 60 days for Curology or $110 to $130 every 60 days for Agency as of October 2026, six shipments a year cost $359.40 to $780. On FutureClinic, a visit is $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100. For a stable medicine like tretinoin, when your doctor judges it safe, one visit can cover several months at once. If you prefer ongoing access for frequent skin questions, most physicians on the platform also have an optional[monthly membership](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) , typically $25 to $100 a month, giving you unlimited care with that doctor that you can cancel any time.


When you and your physician settle on a plan, and if your doctor decides it's right for you, the prescription goes straight to the pharmacy you choose, where your health insurance may cover the fill or the discount coupon FutureClinic texts you can bring down the cash price (and whenever an insurer requires a prior authorization, FutureClinic helps get it). On Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drugs as of October 2026 (with the $5 dispensing fee, before $5.25 shipping), generic tretinoin 0.025% cream is $14.17 (20 g) or $24.63 (45 g), and 0.05% cream is $26.17 (20 g) or $40.19 (45 g). For brand options as of October 2026, Ortho Rx Access lists a $75 cash co-pay (up to 2 fills; excludes Medicare and Medicaid) for 50 g of Retin-A Micro 0.06% or 0.08% gel, and Twyneo's savings card lowers cash cost to as little as $45 (excludes government plans). If your doctor prescribes 0.025% cream and two 45 g tubes last you the year, one $40 visit plus the two tubes from Cost Plus Drugs totals $94.51 with one $5.25 shipment, as of October 2026.
